_comment: Per-session config for scripts/stage7_real_run.py (project_v8 Stage 7: RGB+thermal registration/landmark measurement). Committed, fixed input -- only ever read, like tracking_config.json/analysis_config.json. Only sessions with a real, individually-fit homography AND a human-verified sync_result/entry_time belong here (see project memory project_v8_homography_hybrid_calibration.md for why the other ~35 homography-covered sessions are NOT yet addable: Stage 7 also needs sync offset/drift and a verified entry time, which so far only exist for Test_3/4/7). thermal_seq_relpath/rgb_video_relpath are resolved against --thermal-seq-root/--rgb-video-root at runtime (Alcova-mounted on MedicineBow, a local path when run interactively) -- everything else here is resolved against --repo-dir since it already lives inside the repo's own output directories on every machine.

Test_3.entry_time_note: RGB entry 32.05s converted with the trajectory sync (offset -2.325s, drift +0.00000); was 34.85s under the anchored sync. Tracking starts at frame 349 (re-tracked 2026-10-07 from the old value) -- within 0.5s of this entry, so not re-tracked.

sync_result.confidence_note: 2026-10-08: switched from the hand-anchored sync (offset -2.80s, kept in previous_anchored_sync) to trajectory alignment (scripts/estimate_sync_trajectory.py, MedicineBow validation run; lanes F=-2.30s/drift-0.0000; B=-2.35s/drift-0.0000). Test: Test_7 Stage 7 with the trajectory sync cut moving-sample registration low-confidence 25%->0% (F) and 23%->0% (B), so the anchors (a handful of hand-matched events) were ~0.4-1s off. No anchor fit, so r_squared/residual_max_sec are NaN and sync_passes reads False.

resolved 2026-08-25: 5 real, human-verified anchor events spanning the full session (t=46-2261s thermal), fit AFTER discovering and correcting the camera_fps 8->10 error (see project memory) -- offset is now a clean constant (std=0.13s across all 5 anchors), no drift term needed. Supersedes the earlier -93.0/drift=0 value, which was compensating for the fps error, not real RGB/thermal clock drift. These anchors were all found on the FRONT lane; reused unchanged for Back (2026-08-28) since Front.seq/Back.seq are the same recording.

resolved 2026-08-26: 4 real, human-verified anchor events spanning the full session (t=28-1588s thermal). fps was already 10.0 in this session's tracking data (unlike Test_3/4, no fps correction was needed here -- confirmed via these same anchors: slope=1.00002, implied fps=10.0002). Offset resolved to a tiny near-zero constant, no drift. Homography orientation was separately disputed and resolved: Adam's direct video review initially flagged a Test_4-style 180-degree rotation, but a precise same-real-moment overlay (both centroid AND full mouse silhouette, warped through the as-clicked calibration) landed almost exactly on the real thermal mouse blob including head/tail orientation -- the as-clicked (unmirrored) calibration was confirmed correct; raw RGB-vs-thermal frames are just genuinely hard to compare by eye given the real vertical flip + differing resolution/aspect ratio + the homography's own rotation/perspective terms. These anchors were all found on the FRONT lane; reused unchanged for Back (2026-08-28) since Front.seq/Back.seq are the same recording.
